history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE — Sikh gurdwara complex, keep-or-drop decision needed. Gurudwara Sri Nanaksar Sahib is at village Takhtupura, Moga district (32 km southeast of Moga; 5 km east of Nihal Singhwala; 3 km off the Moga-Barnala road between Lohara and Bilaspur). The CSV town is 'Moga' (the district city); the actual site is village Takhtupura — town corrected. Three shrines, collectively called Nanaksar after the sacred sarovar, commemorate three Gurus: Gurdwara Patshahi Pehli on the sarovar bank (Guru Nanak Dev Ji's discourse with siddha yogis and the Raja Bharthari of Ujjain legend); Gurdwara Patshahi Chhevin (Guru Hargobind Ji, after the Battle of Mehraj 1634, stayed ~45 days; building raised 1921 by Sant Sunder Singh Bhindrawale); Gurdwara Patshahi Dasvin on the eastern bank (Guru Gobind Singh Ji, December 1705, en route Chakar to Dina, bathed in the sarovar; building by Sant Darbara Singh of Lapon, 1962; six-storey marble edifice by Sant Barbara Singh of Lopon, 1975, with lotus dome and gold-plated pinnacle). Note: CSV seq 2043 ('Gurudwara Sahib Patsahi Pehli') is one of this complex's three shrines — likely duplicate/sub-entry of this row.

name: Gurudwara Nanaksar Sahib, Takhtupura
town_description: Takhtupura is a village in Nihal Singhwala tehsil of Moga district, Punjab, about 32 km southeast of Moga city and 3 km off the Moga-Barnala road. It is the site of the Nanaksar Sahib gurdwara complex, which attracts large sangat especially during the January Jor Mela.

travel.airport: Chandigarh International ~120 km; Bathinda airport ~110 km
travel.road: 32 km southeast of Moga via Bagha Purana and Nihal Singhwala, or via Lohara on the Moga-Barnala road; also on Guru Gobind Singh Marg

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Jor Mela (13-17 January) is the biggest annual gathering
